title: Launch after decoding a paired input
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, and let $x,a,b$ be Boolean words such that decoding $x$ gives the pair $(a,b)$. Then there is a time $u \le 5(|x|+1)$ at which the forward simulator on input $x$ is in the virtual configuration representing $M$ initialized on $b$, with boundary tag true, input-head position $|x|+1$, first buffer $a$, and output prefix the encoding of $(a,[])$. Moreover, at every time $v \le u$, the forward and non-forward simulators on $x$ have identical configurations.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over Booleans
